Ituri province accounts for roughly 90% of cases; cases have also appeared in Kisangani and across five other provinces, with cross-border cases identified in Uganda. articleSummary: Indonesia's Ministry of Health warns that chronic liver disease poses a silent killer threat, driven mainly by hepatitis B and C. About 70 million Indonesians are living with chronic liver disease, with global fatalities nearing two million annually, more than half linked to chronic hepatitis B and C. Hepatitis refers to liver inflammation from viral infection, alcohol, drugs, or autoimmune disorders; in Indonesia, hepatitis B and C are principal causes of irreversible liver damage if undetected and untreated early. The condition often shows no early symptoms, with damage accumulating until later liver-related complications. Early warning signs include fatigue, nausea, loss of appetite, right upper quadrant pain, dark urine, jaundice, and abdominal swelling. Preventive measures emphasized: hepatitis B vaccination, routine screening, and risk-reduction strategies like avoiding shared needles; improved education and health services aim to enable earlier diagnosis and reduce mortality from liver failure, cirrhosis, and cancer.

articleSummary: A novel mathematical model of Oropouche virus transmission in Amazonas, Brazil integrates seasonality in midge biting and recruitment across three scenarios: M1 (seasonal biting only), M2 (seasonal recruitment only), and M3 (seasonality in both). Using a next-generation operator framework, the DFE is locally asymptotically stable when R0<1. Parameter values and initial conditions are drawn from literature: human lifespan ~73.43 years, sloth 25 years, midges ~25 days; human/sloth recovery rate 1/4.5 days; NH from 2022 census; NA estimated from sloth density 1.7/km2 times Amazonas area. Initial conditions: IH(0)=0; IF(0)=IC(0)=0. Initial city midge population in Manaus ~137,000, inferred from Porto Velho data. Weekly incidence data from May 28, 2023 to June 1, 2024 (MOH) are used, with 40% symptomatic assumed, incidence scaled to prevalence. Estimated parameters include bπ_VH, bπ_HV, k, ΛF, ΛC, and seasonality parameters t*, a, v, α, β, plus r_A, r_F.

articleSummary: First report of Angiostrongylus vasorum infecting a lesser grison (Galictis cuja) in Brazil. A. vasorum, a metastrongylid nematode known as the 'French heartworm,' parasitizes pulmonary arteries and the right heart and causes canine angiostrongylosis with respiratory and cardiovascular involvement. In Brazil, infections have been reported mainly in domestic dogs and some wild canids; this study documents the first mustelid host record in the country, found after being run over on a southern Brazilian highway. Fecal examinations revealed larvae; identification was morphometric and molecular via PCR targeting COX1, with sequencing and phylogenetic analysis confirming A. vasorum at 99–100% identity to GenBank sequences. This expands the known host range and adds a South American sequence. The authors note the indirect life cycle with terrestrial gastropods as intermediate hosts and transmission through ingestion of infected snails or paratenic hosts; underline wildlife surveillance for emerging helminths.

articleSummary: Ancient plague expansion: Yersinia pestis genomes recovered from 3 prehistoric samples, including East Asia, from 8,000–400 cal. BP, among 1,400 screened remains. By combining these with 136 published ancient and modern genomes, researchers resolve a trans‑Eurasian polytomy dated to ~5.3 ka BP linking Scandinavia, Central Europe, and northern China. The low SNP distances and tip-dating indicate splits over century‑scale intervals across >7,500 km, with a median dispersal rate of 32.9 km yr⁻¹, consistent with rapid long‑distance spread. Mapping variation onto the deep phylogeny shows the basal stem of the LNBA+ lineage uniquely enriched for disruptive remodeling (including acquisition of the ymt gene and multiple gene‑disrupting indels and gene losses), suggesting an early adaptation event tied to later flea‑adapted lineages. The findings extend the prehistoric plague record into East Asia and refine the timing and scale of its earliest trans‑Eurasian expansion.

articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpassed 1,000 deaths 67 days after declaration on May 15, 2026. As of July 21, 2026, 2,536 confirmed cases, 1,033 deaths and 506 recoveries; 63 new cases and 34 new deaths; 306 suspected, 738 in isolation. Ituri accounts for about 90% of cases and over 80% of deaths. No licensed vaccine or treatment exists; surveillance is limited (82% of identified contacts traced; WHO target 90–95%; Africa CDC notes fewer than 9% monitored). In late June, an Ebola treatment centre in Ituri was attacked and set on fire, killing two people. A Bundibugyo clade with 219 SNPs; Oxford began Phase I Bundibugyo vaccine trial on July 13; Ervebo guidance remains cautious.

articleSummary: Costa Rica receives 6,800 units of leishmaniasis treatment donated by Panama, Brazil, and Peru to address drug shortages as the country reports 369 cases in 2026. articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo is escalating, with 2,536 confirmed cases and 1,033 deaths reported; about 738 patients are in treatment centers. The outbreak centers in Ituri Province, including Kisangani, and into Uganda. The active strain is Bundibugyo, for which there are no licensed vaccines or approved therapies. Health authorities say transmission continues, though recent fluctuations may reflect reporting delays and data consolidation. WHO classifies risk as very high in DRC and high in Uganda and neighboring countries, while global risk remains low because transmission occurs by direct contact, not airborne. MSF notes the initial scale was unprecedented; delayed detection allowed wider spread. CDC modeling warns the outbreak could approach the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Response challenges include armed conflict in eastern DRC, displacement, rumors and distrust, health worker strikes over delayed salaries, and that only 77% of known contacts are being followed—far below 95%.
